slice: SOUTH districts discovery wave — District 7 / Phú Mỹ Hưng (Korea Town, expat/international belt), Nhà Bè, and a deepening of District 4 (ốc/seafood + working-class street food). Namespaced SEPARATE from all other SOURCES_HCMC_*.json sets. Yelp/TripAdvisor/Google/Foody/OpenTable contribute 0 toward the source bar.

outlets.name: Saigoneer
outlets.note: Leading English-language Saigon culture/food outlet. Used: dedicated Phú Mỹ Hưng D7 Korea Town walk feature (Perilla); D4 Vĩnh Khánh 'official food street' news feature.

outlets.name: TheSmartLocal Vietnam
outlets.note: Regional lifestyle/food media; '7 Things To Do In Saigon's District 7 For An Authentic Korean Experience' names Perilla (Perilla Seeds Shiraegi) among the D7 Korean picks. Second source for Perilla.

outlets.name: Rusty Compass (Mark Bowyer)
outlets.note: Independent, ad-free Vietnam travel guide. Dedicated Vĩnh Khánh seafood-strip review names Ốc Thảo and Ốc Vũ as the reliable, always-busy houses.

outlets.name: Vietnam Coracle (Tom Divers)
outlets.note: Long-running independent Vietnam travel guide; 'Snails & Shellfish: A Guide' recommends specific Vĩnh Khánh houses (Ốc Oanh, Quán Bé Ốc). Corroborating source for the D4 snail street.

outlets.name: Will Fly for Food (JB & Renée Macatulad)
outlets.note: Established, long-running travel-food blog with a real findable track record; dedicated Vĩnh Khánh street-seafood article naming Ốc Oanh, Ốc Thảo (No. 383) and Ốc Vũ (No. 37). Second source for the two D4 snail houses.

outlets.name: VnExpress International
outlets.note: Vietnam's largest online newspaper (English edition); photo feature on Vĩnh Khánh as 'one of the world's coolest' snail streets. Corroborates the D4 food-street sight.

outlets.name: MICHELIN Guide Vietnam
outlets.note: Referenced only for context: Ốc Oanh (534 Vĩnh Khánh, already in the guide) is the strip's lone MICHELIN Selected / Bib Gourmand snail house; not re-added this wave.
